title: spec: the compactToolbar describe and the userActions liveness note say which toolbar draws Refresh (after #36002)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #36002 (PR #36339). Found by the contract review on PR #36339 (record 7076152814, N2 and N3) and noted by its dev; filed by the seat. Parent: #36002.

## What will be incomplete

PR #36339 makes the `userActions.refresh` describe say it governs only the wide toolbar's Refresh button, and that the default toolbar (the Display form) does not draw one. Two neighbouring texts still read as before:

1. `compactToolbar` in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` is described as "Collapse Group/Color/Density/Hide-fields into a single View settings popover". It says neither which toolbar a renderer draws when the key is omitted nor that the compact toolbar has no Refresh button, so an author or agent cannot tell from the spec which toolbar `userActions.refresh` applies to.
2. The `userActions` note in `packages/spec/liveness/view.json` still says "Sub-key userActions.refresh drives the manual toolbar Refresh button", with no wide-toolbar scope.

## Done when

- The `compactToolbar` describe states the renderer's default and that the compact toolbar draws no Refresh button (pull-to-refresh is unaffected), matching `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` on `main`, with the form hint, regenerated docs and the hint == describe pin kept in step.
- The liveness note names the wide-toolbar scope and the current reader line.
- `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (text only; the accept set does not change).

Blocked-by: #36339 (the new `userActions.refresh` describe must be on `main` first)

## Grade
p3 · area:ux · domain:spec. Describe and audit-note text only; a reader may misjudge which toolbar a flag governs, no behaviour is wrong.
